name: Connecticut
agency: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP)

rule.textEn: Connecticut residents (and owners of property or boats kept in the state, or anyone boating more than 60 days a year) need a Safe Boating Certificate for any registered boat, and a Certificate of Personal Watercraft Operation for a PWC.
rule.textEs: Los residentes de Connecticut (y quienes tienen propiedad o barco en el estado, o navegan más de 60 días al año) necesitan el Safe Boating Certificate para cualquier barco registrado, y el Certificate of Personal Watercraft Operation para una moto acuática.

minAge.note: Under 16 may run a boat other than a PWC uncertified only under direct supervision of a person 18+ certified for at least two years; PWC under 16 only with such a person on board.

exemptions: US Coast Guard master, mate or pilot license (not valid for PWC or towed sports).

card.nameEn: Safe Boating Certificate (SBC) / Certificate of Personal Watercraft Operation (CPWO)
card.feeNote: One-time $50 certificate fee; the DEEP equivalency exam costs $75; a 3-month temporary certificate costs $50; duplicates can be printed free.

nonResident: Visitors need the certificate if their boat must display a Connecticut decal or they boat more than 60 days a year in the state.

sources.quote: Currently there is a onetime fee of $50 for a boating certificate.
The examination fee is $75.00. Testing is by appointment only.
No, asynchronous courses are not approved.
If you are a Connecticut resident operating a registered boat of any kind you must possess a Safe Boating Certificate or Certificate of Personal Watercraft Operation.

By law, any person under the age of 16 may operate a vessel (other than a personal watercraft) without being certified if under the direct supervision of a person 18 or older, who has had their Safe Boating Certificate (SBC) or Certificate of Personal Watercraft Operation (CPWO) for at least two years.
You operate your vessel on CT waters for more than 60 days in a calendar year
